final.question: Why does the safe way have to be the slow way?
final.form: The ISBAR nursing handover sheet — Identify, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation as the five chapters
final.object: Five handover cards, the shape and proportion of her real ISBAR sheet, present throughout and re-arranged chapter to chapter (scattered → stack → row → ring → fan → stack)

swap.reason: The spine is the ISBAR sheet she personally led the redesign of and can show blank, plus her own forty-hour observation and three named workarounds, so the content could not transfer unchanged — though ISBAR itself is common to every Irish nurse, which is the thinnest part of its particularity.

backdrop.reason: The cards are the content carriers — faces hold the text, flips and the old/new toggle live on them, and the stack/row/ring/fan arrangements enact the handover being given and gathered back up, rather than sitting behind the words.

depth.reason: The five chapters follow in a forced order: the question is posed at Identify, the evidence builds through Assessment, and Recommendation answers it and makes the ask.

clipart.reason: The central object is a specific working document she redesigned, not the trade's stock emblem (no stethoscope, scrubs or heart line).

honesty.reason: 71%→94% is captioned "A ward result: pharmacy, IT, the night staff and me," the title reads CNM1 and Link Nurse one day a week, no dashboard outcome is claimed, the whiteboard photo and bed-14 details are absent — only the unattributed hero tag and the unsourced "Built in Power BI" line push past the material.

thirty_seconds.reason: The first screen carries her name, both titles, the hospital, and the 71%→94% proof tag, and the fixed R tab jumps straight to email, CV and LinkedIn.

plain_reader.reason: The opening is plain language — name, role, one number, and a question any reader understands — while ISBAR, the workarounds and the ward-shared credit are the things a nurse or informatics hirer would recognise as real.

judgement.summary: The plan builds the site as an ISBAR handover — five cards shaped like the sheet she redesigned, re-arranged from stack to row to ring to fan and back across five chapters named Identify, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation, opening on "why does the safe way have to be the slow way?" and answering it at the close, with phone, reduced-motion, no-WebGL and no-JS fallbacks, two colour directions and a list of everything else the site needs. Its greatest weakness is that the hero tag "71% → 94% · 9 months" sits on her name card as personal proof several chapters before the line that credits the ward, and one clickable detail ("Built in Power BI, from the ward's own audit data") is an inference presented as fact rather than flagged as an assumption.
